labels: Every rule is a proposed design target unless its note says the vault or the bible establishes it. The owner may edit this file; the next build checks it.

interface.function: resolveStateCulture(model, { owner: { culture, culture2?, faith? }, features: [geography ids] }) in tools/content/lib/cultures_model.mjs (re-exported by modules/cultures.mjs)
interface.returns: { culture, faith, language, minorities: [{ culture, faith, share }], holy_sites: [faith keys], resistance: { target, level, explicit }, rules: [rule ids] }
interface.keys: A rule names a geography feature (an id of tools/content/data/geography/erdae.json: a region, forest, plain, pass, strait, site and so on). States are never named by number, because the map and its states are regenerated. The politics step lists the features that cover each state and passes them in.
interface.order: Rules apply in file order. The first matching enclave rule fixes the state's culture. Every matching mixed rule adds minorities, and the larger share wins. The owner's own second culture adds `owner_second_share`. Minorities together never exceed `max_minority_total`.
interface.owner_filters: `when_owner` lists the owner cultures the rule applies to; `unless_owner` lists those it skips. Without either, the rule applies to every owner.
interface.resistance: Another culture adds 0.20, Great Folk under Common Folk 0.10 and another faith 0.05 (demography spec section 6); the Wall-Folk and Lake Aenorans count as one culture. `owner_resistance` names a level for an owner culture (or `*` for any owner); the larger of the named level and the computed value wins.
interface.startup: stateStartupLines(model, states) writes the on_startup lines that set the state variables zin_state_culture, zin_state_faith and zin_state_culture2 and the state flag zin_holy_site_<faith>.

rules.note: The Cursed Lands resist Aenor totally (demography section 6); the Veiled are an enclave inside Aenor's roads. Established that the Cursed Lands resist Aenor; the culture is proposed.
The Bloody Forest resists Aenor totally. Established that it resists; the culture is proposed.
The Worshipdom's valleys are men inside the elven region (demography section 4).
The Troll Forest is its own country that must stay separate (established); a troll forest under another ruler resists.
Zol's Mistake holds Zol's dead and almost no living people. It does not say who governs the Mistake for Zol (open in the vault).
The Nether is the seat of the King of Demons (established); his name is open.
A few men live at the forest edge and keep its accounts (bible, ents); the Kilinti row of the minor peoples gives them 35 percent.
Ents, men and giants live side by side on the Selen, Kilinti and Hiloron border; any man ruling the forest meets ents who answer to protectors only.
Hilofrim holds men and a small share of giants (demography minor peoples: 4 percent).
Men live beside the giants of Hiloron.
The south marches mix march-folk with refugees from the Dead Lands coast (demography section 6).
The Organ coast road is held by the Bloody Forest side (geography model).
Rangers keep to their wood even under a lowland crown.
Refugees of the Second Age settled the steppe; their descendants are Aenoran in speech and not in habit.
As for the Hunhun Downs.
Refugees of 2A 2133 settled the isle; the houses keep their tide-mothers.
The strait coast is Leren and the inland crowns are Free Crowns.
Leren sailors settle R'en (demography section 6).
The inland crowns prize their independence and accept protection.
Blackton on the Dark Lands coast is mixed Dondor and Leren (demography section 6).
As above, seen from the north shore.
Gunwaith clans and Girdon wardens mix along the Grey Ford, where the Truce was signed.
As above, seen from the south bank.
Buldor companies recruit from every clan (demography section 6).
Guild towns have Aenoran merchants (demography section 6).
Ice clans mix with yeti at the high valleys (demography section 6).
Yeti and giants share the high valleys with the clans.
Windwaith and the western ports have Gunwaithic traders (demography section 6).
Goblins live in orc holds (demography minor peoples: Goldoroth 12 percent, Dulundur 8 percent).
Dondor and Blackton hold human towns beside orc hills; Goldoroth over them meets total resistance (demography section 6).
The sea orcs share islands with Leren fishers (demography section 6).
The rift coast has Alerhic merchants (demography section 6).
Noric and Stabilic peoples mix at the crossroads; a Stabilo-led trade city under Noris resists (demography section 6).
As above, seen from Stabilo.
Caravan towns host every tongue.
The Salt Road carries Stabilic houses into every city it passes.
The Sunfolk of Goodin live among the Sunhot (demography section 6).
The Gala court has a few men and Sunhot courtiers (demography section 6).
Volgan's Dominion holds orcs, ogres and demons beside the dead (demography minor peoples). Ogres have no culture yet; the orc culture is proposed.
Mirolon's wardens and the coast freeholders share the northern passes.
As above, seen from the coast.
